passages.text: By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept when we remembered Zion.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel sat by the rivers of Babylon.
They wept there.
They remembered Zion.
They felt sorrow as they thought of their homeland.
passages.original: עַ֥ל נַהֲר֨וֹת׀ בָּבֶ֗ל שָׁ֣ם יָ֭שַׁבְנוּ גַּם־ בָּכִ֑ינוּ בְּ֝זָכְרֵ֗נוּ אֶת־ צִיּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: There on the willows we hung our harps, for there our captors requested a song; our tormentors demanded songs of joy: “Sing us a song of Zion.”
passages.sermon:
The Israelites sat by the rivers of Babylon.
They were exiles in a foreign land.
They saw willows growing there.
They took their harps.
They hung their harps on the willows.
Their captors came to them.
Their captors asked them for a song.
Their tormentors wanted songs of joy.
Their tormentors said, “Sing us a song of Zion.”
passages.original: עַֽל־ עֲרָבִ֥ים בְּתוֹכָ֑הּ תָּ֝לִ֗ינוּ כִּנֹּרוֹתֵֽינוּ׃ כִּ֤י שָׁ֨ם שְֽׁאֵל֪וּנוּ שׁוֹבֵ֡ינוּ דִּבְרֵי־ שִׁ֭יר וְתוֹלָלֵ֣ינוּ שִׂמְחָ֑ה שִׁ֥ירוּ לָ֝֗נוּ מִשִּׁ֥יר צִיּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: How can we sing a song of the LORD in a foreign land?
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel lived in exile in Babylon.
They remembered their home in Jerusalem.
They felt deep sorrow.
Their captors asked them to sing songs of joy.
The Israelites asked a question.
They said, “How can we sing a song of the LORD?”
They said, “We are in a foreign land.”
passages.original: אֵ֗יךְ נָשִׁ֥יר אֶת־ שִׁיר־ יְהוָ֑ה עַ֝֗ל אַדְמַ֥ת נֵכָֽר׃

passages.text: If I forget you, O Jerusalem, may my right hand cease to function.
passages.sermon: The speaker is an Israelite in exile.\r\nThe Israelite addresses Jerusalem.\r\nThe Israelite says, “If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand lose its strength.”

passages.text: May my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you, if I do not exalt Jerusalem as my greatest joy!
passages.sermon:
The speaker is an Israelite in exile.
The speaker addresses Jerusalem.
The speaker says, "May my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you."
The speaker says, "May this happen if I do not make Jerusalem my highest joy."
The speaker declares that Jerusalem is his greatest happiness.
The speaker promises never to forget Jerusalem.
passages.original: תִּדְבַּ֥ק־ לְשׁוֹנִ֨י׀ לְחִכִּי֮ אִם־ לֹ֪א אֶ֫זְכְּרֵ֥כִי אִם־ לֹ֣א אַ֭עֲלֶה אֶת־ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֑ם עַ֝֗ל רֹ֣אשׁ שִׂמְחָתִֽי׃

passages.text: Remember, O LORD, the sons of Edom on the day Jerusalem fell: “Destroy it,” they said, “tear it down to its foundations!”
passages.sermon:
David speaks in this psalm.
He addresses the Lord.
He asks God to remember the sons of Edom.
The sons of Edom acted on the day Jerusalem fell.
They spoke against Jerusalem.
They said, “Destroy it.”
They said, “Tear it down to its foundations.”
passages.original: זְכֹ֤ר יְהוָ֨ה׀ לִבְנֵ֬י אֱד֗וֹם אֵת֮ י֤וֹם יְֽרוּשָׁ֫לִָ֥ם הָ֭אֹ֣מְרִים עָ֤רוּ׀ עָ֑רוּ עַ֝֗ד הַיְס֥וֹד בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: O Daughter of Babylon, doomed to destruction, blessed is he who repays you as you have done to us.
passages.sermon:
The Daughter of Babylon is a nation.
Babylon faces destruction.
Someone will repay Babylon.
Babylon did evil to us.
Blessed is the one who repays Babylon.
He will repay Babylon for what Babylon did to us.
passages.original: בַּת־ בָּבֶ֗ל הַשְּׁד֫וּדָ֥ה אַשְׁרֵ֥י שֶׁיְשַׁלֶּם־ לָ֑ךְ אֶת־ גְּ֝מוּלֵ֗ךְ שֶׁגָּמַ֥לְתְּ לָֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Blessed is he who seizes your infants and dashes them against the rocks.
passages.sermon:
This verse speaks about the enemies of Israel, specifically Babylon.
Babylon destroyed Jerusalem and caused great suffering.
The verse describes a person who takes Babylon’s infants.
This person seizes the infants.
He dashes the infants against the rocks.
The verse calls this person blessed.
passages.original: אַשְׁרֵ֤י׀ שֶׁיֹּאחֵ֓ז וְנִפֵּ֬ץ אֶֽת־ עֹ֝לָלַ֗יִךְ אֶל־ הַסָּֽלַע׃
